rule.title: FAIR Act - Prohibition on Property Owners Using Coordinator Services
rule.requirement: It is unlawful and a violation of the New Jersey Antitrust Act for a rental property owner, or any agent, representative, or subcontractor thereof, to receive, subscribe to, contract for, or otherwise exchange any form of consideration in return for the use of, the services of a coordinator.
rule.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental property owners (persons that own, directly or indirectly, one or more rental residential dwelling units) or any agent, representative, or subcontractor thereof.
rule.exemptions: Residential dwelling units exclude inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, or detention or correctional facilities. Coordinators exclude government entities setting or limiting rents or sale prices through affordability controls.
rule.interaction: Provides that violations constitute a violation of the New Jersey Antitrust Act, P.L.1970, c.73 (C.56:9-1 et seq.). Section 5 provides that the act does not limit the application of sections 6 through 17 of P.L.1970, c.73. Section 6(a) states the act is in addition to the New Jersey Antitrust Act. Section 6(b) prohibits municipalities from enacting conflicting ordinances.

rule.title: FAIR Act - Prohibition on Coordinators Facilitating Anticompetitive Agreements
rule.requirement: A coordinator is prohibited from facilitating a tacit or express agreement among rental property owners that restricts competition with respect to residential dwelling units, including by performing a coordinating function.
rule.coverage_conditions: Applies to coordinators operating algorithmic revenue management software or an algorithmic device that performs a coordinating function for any rental property owner.
rule.exemptions: Excludes government entities setting or limiting rents or sale prices through affordability controls in accordance with law. Coordinating function excludes research/testing not used in setting lease terms, free public rent estimates, qualifying brokerage databases, and government affordability controls.
rule.interaction: Governed by the introductory clause of Section 4 establishing violations as violations of the New Jersey Antitrust Act, P.L.1970, c.73 (C.56:9-1 et seq.). Section 6(b) prohibits municipalities from enacting conflicting ordinances.
